text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- All newspapers front Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim reiterating that there was a delay in the $6.18 billion Bakun hydroelectric project, brushing aside claims by main contractor Ekran chairman Ting Pek Khiing there was no major dispute with construction contractor ABB Asea Brown Boveri

-- Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said the ringgit's exchange rate was still manageable after the local unit slipped more than 3.2 percent this week to 2.59 a dollar. It fell from 2.56 level to its current level on Wednesday evening.
-- A change in the ownership of Datuk Keramat Holdings Bhd and its subsidiary George Town Holdings Bhd will not affect the composition of its management and board of directors.
-- Sapura Motors Bhd expects a sharp improvement in its performance due to a buoyancy in the vehicle market and its own efforts to diversify its customer base.
